1. Need to remove bonding screw. The nuetrals and grounds should be bonded only at the first means of disconnect.
2. 1/2" knockout seal on the top.
3. Bushing on wire size larger than #4 entering top.
4. Couple ground wires not terminated.
5. Looks like there wasn't any de-ox used on the aluminum terminations. Maybe I'm wrong.

That is very close to a finish piece. About 1 minute away. It's missing the 2 lugs that are needed to land the 2 large ground wires, and the parts I mentioned. It's has to be done right before you can worry about how pretty it is. No one likes unlanding wires to put on a bushing they forgot. Especially when they are already zip tied down.

items.title: First ReefTank 2 month update.
items.text: First ReefTank 2 month update.

Just started my refugium this week. Using sea lettuce. The diatoms have been present for a month and the cyano is starting in a couple dead spots, but I since have increased flow and will do the first gravel vac when I do a wc this weekend. I have been putting it off. 
I am loving the change from my freshwater planted tanks. It's been a couple of years in the planning, and it isn't a finished project. I do have nice cabinet doors that I am in the process of staining to cover the stand. I still need to get an ato, and I am sure things will come up that I need.
Is there any advice or tips anyone would like to share?

40 gallon breeder, with 40 gallon breeder sump. 2x kessil a160we with kessil spectral controller. 150w led grow light in fuge. Fuge is about 13 gallons. Flow is controlled with a valve from my return pump(sicce 3.0) Used the glass holes 700gph overflow kit. It's kind of loud, not terrible Uses 1-1/2" black flexible PVC for drain. Black 3/4" pvc return and it splits into 2 3/4" locline nozzles. 2-300 watt Eheim jagger heaters (Need a controller). Running a Vertex Omega 130 skimmer which I really like. DIY the sump baffles using 6mm thick glass. Brs dry rock, figi pink live sand.
40 gallon breeder at Petco $/gallon sale. Now easily over 3k in.

I ended up getting 2 Kessil a160we's. Mounted on two of the a-series mounting arms. Controlled by the sprectral controller. It's was the most expensive part of the build. I could have spent less but really like the shimmer and the sophisticated look of the kessil lights and arms.

Pixel 2 lol. I have 4 slab cabinet doors that attach with magnets. I am in the process of staining them. I wanted to paint them, and kind of mimic a redsea reefer. But after I came home with the doors, the wife saw them and wanted stain.  So now I have a nice weathered grey stain to match the quartz top.

It has a lot to do with the surface agitation. If the surface is really broken up there will be almost too much. My son that is in high school has 2 prime hd's, and it is similar. But they don't blend the colors as well and it you can see the multiple colors dance around. I am debating eventually supplementing t5s to give the best of both worlds.

I used a kit from glass holes. It was the 700 gph overflow box. It was cheap but I am k/of wishjng I went with the eschopps overflow. I am sure it would have been a little quieter. In the end I went with the kit because it had everything I needed and I could order PVC parts from them that we're black. The only problem with the glass holes overflow is the basic design. They have done everything they can to make that design work. it just is inherently louder than a full siphon drain.

 That is the one I'm saving for next!

I 100% agree with you. If I had a apprentice, or even a journeyman working for me doing this- without being specifically asked to- I would tell them to quit that shit and get it done quickly.
I'd like to see at least 6 inches of wire inside that panel before terminating.
Panel is only good for 20-25 years. The next guy will curse you.
Also how is that panel supported? It looks like it has every knockout on both sides? It may be better to practice coming through the top/bottom. That is more typical in the field.
Ok. In my area if it's under 7' it needs protected by conduit.
Well the ones you install in the field will be new. And after 25 years someone will come and replace the panel you put in. That guy will curse you because the wire is 3" long.

I would come in the top of the panel so I didn't have nm cable under 7'. But if I had to come in the  side, I would sleeve it in conduit, then either terminate on a screw that allows me at least 6" of wire inside the box or leave a loop. What happens when a wire burns up on the end? You have no wire to trim off,and it won't reach anything.

Happening to me in my wrx with 30k miles. Really disappointed in the quality of the materials used. In 10 years every newer Subaru will have a completely trashed steering wheel to match their shitty paint, and shitty leather seats. It's a love hate/thing with my wrx.
Also the Perrin shifter bushing/shift stop/ heavy shift knob all work very well together to deliver a much better feel shifting gears.
I've never heard anyone change that much water. Unless they were really trying to dilute something in their water, or fed a ton of food. 25% once a week is good I think.

The brass bushing replaces a cheap rubber bushing. It gives it more of a click-clack feeling. & The shift stop reduces the amount of slop in between each gear. For instance put you car in 1st gear, and then wiggle it back and forth. It moves around 1" each way. With the stop in place it moves like 1/4 to an 1/8 of an inch. Can't recommend enough.

Limited are black. Base is chrome. Iirc

I would try and find a complete setup that is used. Or go with a all in one style tank. Otherwise you could easily spend double, triple, or even possibly quadruple your budget on the tank and getting it running using all nice new stuff. I have well over $3k (closer to 4)in my 40 breeder tank. It is only about 3 months old. I have 2 fish and 4 coral frags. I have no automation. Still need an auto top off, another powerhead, better testing equipment, copepods and macro algae to start my fuge, and the list goes on. I could spend another $1200 today :) this hobby is very expensive.

In my area it is required. Ahj doesn't see any difference because it is there to protect the wire after being pulled as well as during. I don't put to much time into interpretation of the codes. I just care mostly about what the inspector wants to see. Sheathing inside the panel is a code requirement -I think it is at least 1/4 " required.

Bonding screw needs removed. Grounds and nuetrals shall be bonded at 1st means of disconnect. This is a sub panel. That and the and 1/2" knockout on top. But yeah other then the 4 or 5 violations he would have passed an inspection here.
